question: Resuming the y72fix2 run at update 300 (per-task clip 0.5, replay weight 0.25 unchanged), does replaying rows from a fresh pre-registered 200-row Y72 pool, each row exactly once, keep Y72 held on the 600-segment set while X64 keeps progressing through update 400? (pre-registered as vyra-y72-rehearsal2-fresh-v1)
design: One run, one seed, resume from the update-300 checkpoint (sha256 verified before load; the restored model reproduced the recorded integer counts at 300 exactly, tolerance 0), updates 301..400. The only change from the cont400 run is the replay rows: update s+1 uses pool rows 2*(s-300) and 2*(s-300)+1, so all 200 pool rows are used once. Evaluation and full checkpoints at 325/350/375/400; gates at 350/375/400 (the cont400 gates, unchanged). Free Kaggle T4 x2, no retries.

setup.dataset_mounts: all three datasets were found by file hash at a different mount layout than the pinned one, then re-hashed by the dependency gate (59 files)

R_hold.rule: sum over 350/375/400 of Y72 (600-set) >= 1440 and each >= 432

A_progress.rule: X64 held-out >= 44/240 at each gate checkpoint and tokens at 400 >= 1723/1920 (+3.0 pp from 1665)

N_nonregression.rule: X32 >= 128/320 and X109 >= 90/120 at each gate checkpoint

final.observation_non_gating: Y72 (600-set) rose monotonically 569/573/592/595 and X64 held-out exact rose 26/85/147/150 at 325/350/375/400. The non-gating manipulation checks M1 and M2 fail only in the last window 376-400 (median replay pull 0.0735 < 0.10, median replay loss 0.0036 < 0.005): by then the fresh rows were largely fitted, which the prereg anticipated as a possible M2 failure. M3 (each pool row once) holds.

verdict: SUCCESS on the pre-registered gates. R passes (Y72 573/592/595, sum 1760 >= 1440, each >= 432), A passes (X64 held-out exact 85/147/150 >= 44, tokens at 400 1798 >= 1723, +6.9 pp), N passes. One run, one seed.
limitations: one seed, one run, no retry
the non-gating M1/M2 checks fail in the final window, so the replay signal was weak over 376-400
the earlier cont400 run showed large checkpoint-to-checkpoint swings; this run's monotone trajectory is one sample

cost.gpu_hours_kaggle_quota_displayed: about 0.16 (22.79 h -> 22.95 h of 30 h, two rounded displays)
